cap: The perineal membrane spans the ischiopubic rami and divides the urogenital triangle: the deep pouch above holds the external urethral sphincter, membranous urethra and bulbourethral glands; the superficial pouch below holds the bulb, which continues as the corpus spongiosum, the crura and their muscles, and in women the Bartholin glands, whose ducts open at the posterolateral vaginal orifice. A spongy urethral tear spreads under Colles fascia to the scrotum, penis and abdominal wall, but not the thighs; a membranous tear leaks into the retropubic space.
